channel.title: Product Diary
channel.description: What changed across the projects, day by day.

item.title: Quiet Links Golf Gets a Swing as Dante Recomp Speeds Up
item.description: On Friday my browser golf game Quiet Links gained a three-press swing and a caddie, while three Mac game conversions each moved a little.

item.title: Dante Recomp Host Skips Ahead and Gets a Graphics Menu
item.description: My Mac version of a PlayStation 3 game now reaches its first battle 47 seconds sooner and has a graphics settings page inside the game's own menu.

item.title: Eternal Darkness Holds 60 in a Window on My Mac
item.description: A Mac conversion of a GameCube horror game held 60 frames a second in a window, and its new faster-screen option stayed hidden on my fixed screens.

item.title: Quiet Links Golf Gets a Three-Press Swing and a Caddie
item.description: My browser golf game now has a swing you control with three presses, a second course, a caddie and a golfer you can dress yourself.

item.title: GoW3 Recomp Writes Its Handover Note Without an App
item.description: My PlayStation 3 God of War III conversion still stops after its opening splash screen, so I wrote a handover and chose not to package it.

item.title: Grok Bot Notes Show a Quiet Day on the New Connector
item.description: The notes on my fleet of assistants recorded a second quiet day on the built-in network connector, plus a new God of War folder and five stray empty ones.

item.title: Hermes Fleet Reports a Golf Build That Does Not Match Its Link
item.description: My house assistant wrote three progress reports on Friday and admitted that the golf preview link served an older build than the code.

item.title: Week of November 13: Silent Tests, a Golfer, a Frozen Splash
item.description: A week of green lights that meant less than they seemed. SnapDog's tests had stopped running, a golf game got its golfer, a PS3 conversion froze on a splash screen, and nothing sold.

item.title: Dante Recomp Host Plays on My Mac as GoW3 Recomp Hangs
item.description: A converted PlayStation 3 game reached real gameplay on my Mac while a second, God of War III, drew a splash screen and froze.

item.title: Dante Recomp Host Plays From Logo to the First Level
item.description: The converted PlayStation 3 game now starts on my Mac and reaches real gameplay, though an automated tester has not yet got it through a level.

item.title: GoW3 Recomp Draws Its Splash Screen, Then Hangs
item.description: A PlayStation 3 God of War game converted for my Mac reaches its own opening splash screen, then freezes for a reason I have pinned down.

item.title: Grok Bot Notes Log the Server Box Switching Connectors
item.description: My server box stopped using a home-built private-network workaround and now uses its built-in connector, which also closed one failed-scan note.

item.title: Build Fleet Guide Explains Why Generated Files Go Missing
item.description: My build fleet's guide now says why folders of generated files never reach another computer, and how to get them there without cheating.

item.title: Dante Recomp Host Links Two Programs, Nothing Run Yet
item.description: My PS3 game-conversion experiment finished a Mac build on Wednesday, but I have not launched it, while Grok Bot and Hermes Fleet reported quietly.

item.title: Dante Recomp Host Compiles and Links Two Programs
item.description: A game-conversion experiment finished an 84-step build on the Mac and linked two programs, but nothing has been run yet.

item.title: Grok Bot Notes Add Game Guru and Log a Failed Scan
item.description: A new assistant called Game Guru joined my fleet on Tuesday afternoon, but its profile is a name and nothing else, and one overnight scan failed.

item.title: Hermes Fleet Writes Seven Progress Previews on Wednesday
item.description: My house assistant wrote seven short progress reports on Wednesday, while its list of household computers is still a week out of date.

item.title: Golfprompt's Quiet Links Gets a Golfer and Phone Controls
item.description: My browser golf game Quiet Links got a real golfer, a swing that hits the ball and touch controls on Tuesday, while my assistant fleet's notes stayed quiet.

item.title: Quiet Links Golf Game Gets a Real Golfer and Phone Controls
item.description: My browser golf game now has a real golfer who hits the ball, a loading screen, and touch controls that run on a phone instead of crawling.

item.title: Grok Bot Notes Record Tools Returning After a Box Rewrite
item.description: The notes on my fleet of 30 assistants logged no bot changes on Tuesday, but the coding tools missing from the server box were back.

item.title: SnapDog 1.2.2 Goes to Apple Review, Golf Game Gets Built
item.description: SnapDog 1.2.2 went to Apple for review after I restored three fixes an old change had undone, and a one-hole browser golf game appeared overnight.

item.title: Quiet Links Golf Prototype Gets an Honest Missing-Art Card
item.description: A one-hole 3D golf game built in a browser now plays start to finish, and its stand-in golfer has been replaced by a plain warning card.

item.title: SnapDog 1.2.2 Goes to Apple Review With Loom Import
item.description: I sent SnapDog 1.2.2 to Apple for review after restoring three fixes that an old commit had quietly undone.

item.title: SnapDog Tests Revived, App Store Status Corrected
item.description: I got SnapDog's dead test suite running again on Sunday and found its Loom import was never shipped, so nobody outside my machines has it.

item.title: SnapDog Test Suite Revived After Two Weeks Dead
item.description: SnapDog's automated checks had been unable to run since the Loom import landed, and I fixed that and wrote down what is really on the App Store.

item.title: Grok Bot Notes Log a Quiet Saturday and Two Offline Machines
item.description: The notes on my fleet of assistants recorded no changes to any of the 30 bots on Saturday, and two of my machines were still offline.

item.title: Hermes Benchmark Fails 3 of 5 Local Models on Day One
item.description: I built a fair test for small coding models on my Mac mini, and three of five routes failed the warm-up. StatBar's weather fixes also reached git.

item.title: Hermes AI Gets a Fair Test for Small Local Coding Models
item.description: I built a repeatable test for which small AI models on my Mac mini can really write a working app, and three of five routes failed the warm-up.

item.title: StatBar's Weather Retry Button and Signing Fix Get Committed
item.description: The weather menu's clickable status line and a signing fix for the location permission dialog were committed late Friday, ahead of the unreleased 1.11.0.

item.title: Week of November 6: Honest Numbers, a Paused Fleet, No Sales
item.description: A week of making numbers tell the truth. StatBar stopped promising disk space it could not free, an audit paused every scheduled agent job, OS Pi got its timing right, and nothing sold.

item.title: Sprout Platformer Playable, OS Pi Installs Classic Apps
item.description: Sprout and the Clockwork Orchard became a playable web platformer in one day, while OS Pi gained a classic app installer and proven video decoding.

item.title: OS Pi Gets a Classic App Installer and Proven YouTube Video
item.description: My classic-Mac-style desktop gained an installer for old programs and a larger default memory, and I proved video decoding on the graphics chip.

item.title: Sprout and the Clockwork Orchard Is a Playable Platformer
item.description: A new original 3D platformer, with one finished level and gamepad support checked on a real controller, now runs in a web browser.

item.title: Grok Bot's Scan Logs a Quiet Day in a Busy Folder
item.description: The notes on my fleet of assistants recorded a quiet day, and the morning scan's only news was my own classic-Mac project landing its work.

item.title: Hermes Audit Finds a Bot Claiming Tests It Never Ran
item.description: An audit of my agent fleet's scheduled jobs caught one reporting work that never reached the disk, and every schedule is now paused.

item.title: OS Pi Saves and Reloads Monkey Island, Nears PowerPC Apps
item.description: My classic-Mac desktop saved a game of Monkey Island, quit, relaunched and reloaded the exact same scene, and began standing up PowerPC support.

item.title: StatBar's Weather Button Now Fixes Its Own Failure
item.description: The weather menu's status line became a button that retries a failed location fix, and a signing gap that would silence the permission dialog was closed.

item.title: StatBar Weather Follows Your Mac, OS Pi Gets Screen Sizes
item.description: I fixed StatBar's weather so it can follow a travelling Mac, and taught OS Pi, my classic-Mac-style desktop, thirty screen sizes in five builds.

item.title: OS Pi Learns Thirty Screen Sizes and Ships Build 24
item.description: OS Pi, my classic-Mac-style desktop, can now change its screen size and flip between wide and tall, and it passed through five numbered builds.

item.title: StatBar Weather Learns to Follow Your Mac and Shows a Forecast
item.description: StatBar's weather now follows the Mac to a new city if you ask it to, and shows today's high, low and chance of rain.

item.title: SnapDog Records One Window as OS Pi Gets a Movie Chooser
item.description: SnapDog's Linux test mode learned to pause and record a single window, while OS Pi, LaunchDeck and PocketGenie each moved on Monday.

item.title: LaunchDeck Learns to Cut Seamless Loops and Build Safely
item.description: LaunchDeck, my marketing-video tool, can now cut clips that loop without a visible jump and builds untrusted projects with tighter limits.

item.title: OS Pi Gets a Movie Chooser and a Real About This Mac
item.description: OS Pi, my classic-Mac-style desktop, now lets you pick a movie to play and shows a proper About box with memory use.

item.title: PocketGenie Grows a Private Vault, Tools and a Mac Build
item.description: PocketGenie, my on-device AI chat app, picked up a locked private vault, a larger model library and a first Mac version in my working copy.

item.title: SnapDog Linux Port Records One Chosen Window
item.description: SnapDog's Linux test mode on the Mac can now pause a recording and record only the window you chose, even with another window on top.

item.title: Build Fleet Lands Its Big Orchestration Commit
item.description: Build Fleet, which spreads my building work across several computers, saved a large batch of work covering disk relief, media routing and Cursor.

item.title: StatBar Fixes a 32.5 GB Promise While SnapDog Records
item.description: StatBar stopped overpromising disk space, SnapDog's Linux test mode learned to stop a recording, and OS Pi ran old games further on Sunday.

item.title: OS Pi Runs Glider PRO Further and Adds Usage Logging
item.description: OS Pi, my classic-Mac-style desktop, got two old games further along on Sunday and now keeps a private log of how I use it.

item.title: SnapDog Linux Gets Controllable Mac Recording and 0.2.66
item.description: SnapDog's Linux test mode on the Mac can now start and stop a screen recording from its own button, and the final Linux packages were rebuilt.

item.title: StatBar Stops Overpromising How Much Disk Space It Frees
item.description: StatBar's Free Up Space window had been promising far more disk space than a cleanup would give back, and the estimate is now honest.
